requirement:
The Habeas crate MUST have a Cargo integration test that exercises evidence
authoring against a real configured Bedrock model when AWS credentials can be
loaded. It MUST skip before reading configuration or resolving credentials when
the `CI` environment variable is present. Outside CI, it MUST fail when no
Bedrock authoring configuration exists, and MUST skip with a visible warning when
the AWS SDK cannot load credentials. Skip warnings MUST be visible under ordinary
`cargo test` output.

`HABEAS_LIVE_CONFIG`, when set, MUST select a named authoring configuration for
the test. Otherwise the test MUST use the configuration that authoring would
select for the checkout under {cite}`requirements.authoring.configuration_precedence`
when it is a Bedrock configuration, falling back to the first Bedrock
configuration in name order among the user and workspace configurations. The
fixture project MUST resolve the selected name against the same workspace
authoring configurations as the checkout. Malformed configuration and invalid explicit
selections MUST fail the test. The selected profile, region, model, and options
MUST come from that configuration; credential resolution MUST use the AWS SDK.

Once credentials load, model-request and authoring failures MUST fail the test
rather than be treated as skips. The test MUST exercise an additional source read
and judgment submission using a temporary project and stdout evidence output,
without changing the checkout's evidence. It MUST retain ordinary usage history
and check the returned evidence and recorded usage. Deterministic tests MUST
verify the CI and missing-credential skip paths and the missing-configuration
failure without calling a model.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider`
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`
{cite}`requirements.authoring.submission`
{cite}`requirements.authoring.persistence`
{cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_storage`
rationale:
structural: Only one clause prescribes how the test is built: "credential resolution MUST use the AWS SDK." The root `tests/live_bedrock.rs#fn[credentials_available]` carries that clause. It builds an `aws_config::defaults(...)` loader and applies the configuration's `aws_profile` and `region`. It then loads the SDK config and calls `provider.provide_credentials()` on the SDK's credentials provider. A hand-written credential lookup, such as reading environment variables or credential files directly, could skip the same cases but would violate the clause. So this clause needs implementation evidence, and the root supplies it. It is also the only code that resolves credentials: `live_bedrock_authoring` calls it and does no resolution of its own.

The other clauses describe observable behavior:
- **Cargo integration test:** a file under `tests/` is an integration test by location. The requirement names no library or type for it.
- **CI skip, missing-configuration failure and missing-credential skip:** these are behaviors that `live_bedrock_authoring` and `skip_probe` can show. The ordering (skip before reading configuration) is observable.
- **Configuration selection** (`HABEAS_LIVE_CONFIG`, authoring precedence, name-order fallback, same workspace configurations): `select_config` and `selected_config` implement this. The text only requires the selection outcome. Reusing the authoring resolver or reimplementing the precedence would behave the same, so how it is built is discretionary. These functions are marked `{test}` for `requirements.authoring.configuration_precedence`.
- **Profile, region, model and options come from the configuration:** `credentials_available` takes the selected `BedrockConfig`. The test passes `--config` to the spawned `habeas` binary. This is behavior that tests can check.
- **Authoring failures fail the test; temporary project, stdout output, unchanged checkout evidence, usage checks:** all are behavioral and checked through assertions in `live_bedrock_authoring`.
- **Cited requirements** (`requirements.authoring.provider`, `requirements.authoring.source_tools`, `requirements.authoring.submission`, `requirements.authoring.persistence`, `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`): these supply context only.

No further structural obligation lacks an implementation root.

behavioral: The reviewed tests adequately cover every obligation of `requirements.integration.live_bedrock_test`. I found no gaps and no marking gaps.

The obligations are mapped to tests below. Each deterministic scenario runs the real `live_bedrock_authoring` test as a child process through `skip_probe`. `skip_probe` clears the `AWS_*` variables, `CI` and `HABEAS_LIVE_CONFIG`. It points the config and state directories and the AWS config files at a temporary directory, and it points the Bedrock endpoint at a dead local address, so no model is called.

**Skip when `CI` is present, before reading configuration.**
- `live_test_prerequisites_are_checked_without_inference` writes a malformed user config and sets `CI=true`.
- It asserts that the child exits successfully and that stderr contains "skipping live Bedrock test: CI is set".
- Success despite the malformed config shows the skip happens before configuration is read.
- The same malformed config without `CI` fails with "cannot select live Bedrock configuration".

**Fail outside CI when no Bedrock authoring configuration exists.**
- Three cases are tested: no config file, a config with no authoring section, and a config with only an Ollama configuration.
- Each must exit non-zero with "no Bedrock authoring configuration", and stderr must not contain the skip text.
- `live_configuration_selection_follows_authoring_precedence` also asserts that `select_config` returns `None` for these inputs.

**Skip with a visible warning when the AWS SDK cannot load credentials.**
- A Bedrock configuration with an empty credentials file must exit successfully with "AWS credentials unavailable" in stderr, and no `Usage:` line.
- The warning is written by `report` straight to stderr. The child runs without `--nocapture`, so the assertion shows it is visible under ordinary `cargo test` output.

**`HABEAS_LIVE_CONFIG` selects a named configuration, and invalid selections fail.**
- An env value of "missing" with no config file must fail with "cannot select live Bedrock configuration". That differs from the no-config message, so it shows `selected_config` reads the variable.
- `select_config` explicit-name cases cover an explicit name beating project, workspace and default selections, a non-Bedrock explicit name ("must select a Bedrock configuration"), and an unknown name.
- Malformed user config (`[authoring`) and malformed workspace config (`version = [`) are both asserted to be errors.

**Default selection follows `requirements.authoring.configuration_precedence`, then falls back to the first Bedrock configuration in name order.**
- The precedence test covers the user's project selection winning over the default.
- It covers the workspace default sitting between the project selection and the user default.
- It covers a Bedrock user default being used, and an Ollama default (`aaa-local`) falling back to the first Bedrock configuration, `alpha`.
- It covers workspace-only configurations, and name ordering across user and workspace configurations (`aaa` from the workspace versus `beta` from the user).
- The result for `alpha` is checked field by field: model, `aws_profile`, `region` and `options` all come from the selected record.

**The fixture project resolves against the same workspace authoring configurations.**
- The test parses `selection.workspace` and checks that `authoring.configs.gamma.model` is present.
- It also checks that unrelated sections such as `evidence` are dropped.
- Writing that content into the fixture is part of the live test.

**Credential resolution uses the AWS SDK.** `credentials_available` uses `aws_config` with the selected profile and region. The skip-path tests check its outcomes for missing and fake credentials.

**After credentials load, model-request and authoring failures fail the test.** The test supplies fake AWS keys and a dead endpoint. The child must exit non-zero, report "live Bedrock test: configuration", print "live Bedrock authoring failed" on stdout, and not print the skip text.

**The live run itself** needs real Bedrock and network access, and no deterministic test can set that up, so it is exempt from separate tests. `live_bedrock_authoring` still asserts everything the requirement lists for it:
- the temporary project is used, with `--stdout`;
- a read-tool input for `src/parity.rs` appears, with a hash and no text;
- the project has no `evidence` directory, and the checkout's evidence snapshot is unchanged;
- the usage record has backend, model, outcome `completed`, `evidence_output` `stdout` and `evidence_written` true, plus tool and attempt counters.

The cited `requirements.authoring.*` requirements are context only, and I did not reassess them.

authoring against a real configured Bedrock model when AWS credentials can be

the test. Otherwise the test MUST use the configuration that authoring would
select for the checkout under {cite}`requirements.authoring.configuration_precedence`
when it is a Bedrock configuration, falling back to the first Bedrock
configuration in name order among the user and workspace configurations. The
fixture project MUST resolve the selected name against the same workspace
authoring configurations as the checkout. Malformed configuration and invalid explicit
selections MUST fail the test. The selected profile, region, model, and options
MUST come from that configuration; credential resolution MUST use the AWS SDK.
Once credentials load, model-request and authoring failures MUST fail the test
rather than be treated as skips. The test MUST exercise an additional source read
and judgment submission using a temporary project and stdout evidence output,
without changing the checkout's evidence. It MUST retain ordinary usage history

failure without calling a model.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider`
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`
{cite}`requirements.authoring.submission`
{cite}`requirements.authoring.persistence`
{cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_storage`
:::{req} configuration_precedence
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
`--config <name>` MUST select a configuration for that invocation. Otherwise,
authoring MUST use the user's selection for the canonical project root, then the
workspace default, then the user's default. Named workspace configurations MUST
override same-named user configurations as complete records. Backend, model,
connection settings, and options MUST come from the selected record as a unit;
fields MUST NOT be merged between records. Workspace-only authoring MUST work
without a user configuration file. Missing configuration or an unknown selection
MUST identify the relevant configuration file and point to documented examples.
An explicit Bedrock AWS profile or region MUST override the corresponding SDK
default; omitted values MUST use standard AWS SDK resolution. Ollama MUST use
its configured endpoint or `http://localhost:11434`. If `api_key_env` is set, its
named variable MUST supply the credential; a missing or empty value MUST produce
an error before a model request. OpenAI MUST use its configured endpoint or
`https://api.openai.com/v1`, and MUST resolve `OPENAI_API_KEY` when neither
`api_key` nor `api_key_env` is supplied.
:::{req} provider
The authoring harness MUST use Rig and support Bedrock, Ollama, and OpenAI. Users MUST be
able to select a backend and model through configuration without changing the
assessment tools, prompt, or evidence format.
:::{req} source_tools

All assessments MUST use the SDK graph and source tools. A read uses the node address under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.mcp`. A delivered read records that node’s fingerprint under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`. The source project follows {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`.
:::{req} submission

Each assessment MUST use the SDK’s `submit_result({"result": ...})` tool under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.mcp`. Requirement and named example assessments MUST submit one variant of a Rust enum:
- `Success { rationale }` records `true`.
- `Failed { corrections }` records `false` and MUST include a nonempty list under {cite}`requirements.authoring.corrections`.
- `AcknowledgedGap { entries, rationale }` records `{"FIXME": entries}` when every real gap is acknowledged under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.

For each non-distributed requirement, Habeas MUST evaluate separate `structural` and `behavioral` criteria in independent conversations. Each submits its own assessment result. The structural criterion may propose `{impl}` markers and the behavioral criterion may propose `{test}` markers. If a submission proposes a marker belonging to the other criterion, request a corrected verdict within scope and reject a repeated violation. Habeas MUST retain both results in `criteria` and compute the overall judgment: failure takes precedence over acknowledged gaps, and both criteria must succeed for success.

Each rationale MUST be nonempty Markdown. Citation reviews submit a boolean `determination` and a rationale. Site reviews submit `determination`, `rationale`, and `applies` under {cite}`requirements.authoring.site_prompt`. The SDK handles submission under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.acceptance`. Failure before acceptance MUST preserve existing evidence.
:::{req} persistence
After policy selection in each round, the harness MUST write the subject text,
mapped determination, rationale, and recorded inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`.
Each of the three outcomes counts as a completed assessment. Its validation
status follows {cite}`requirements.ci.determination`.
:::{req} usage_storage
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
